newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish firms' Oct results extend 4-month uptrend.
newsitem.headline: Polish firms' Oct results extend 4-month uptrend.

text.p: Polish listed firms showed better earnings for the fourth month running in October, but analysts said the rise was too small to offset the weak first half and surprise the market with better-than expected year-end results.
Analysts said the long, harsh winter, which depressed many firms' performance in the first six months, was likely to negatively affect their 1996 results.
"The winter was long and it might have a negative effect on whole year results, especially in the construction sector," said Jacek Dzierwa, an analyst at Salomon Brothers in London.
Analysts said the slower earnings growth reflected also a generally slower economic growth, forecast at about 5.5 percent this year against last year's robust seven percent.
"If the economy's growth is slowing no doubt it will have an effect on listed firms," said Artur Nagorka, an analyst at Wood and Company in Warsaw.
Analysts said the expected weaker 1996 results had already been priced in to a great extent but their impact could still be felt later this year or next.

"They (the financial results) will surely have an impact on the exchange -- if, let's say, a stock rose 60 percent during the year and its profit only 20 percent, it will unpleasantly surprise many investors," Salomon's Dzierwa said.

Some analysts also noted that results for the first 10 months of this year, although an indication of earnings in the whole of 1996, had to be treated cautiously because of possible downward adjustments by auditors in annual earnings reports.
Analysts noted good October reports by BFK, Wedel and Okocim and were disappointed by Zywiec which showed a weak 0.1 million-zloty net profit.
They said Swarzedz's slight net profit after a loss of 33.9 million zlotys earlier in the year gave a hope the company could recover from its financial problems.
Some said listed banks, the bourse's heavyweights, were likely to show good results for the whole year as the sector so far showed stable growth, despite a weaker October.
"Banks are the most stable sector: they don't show jumps but there are no unpleasant surprises either," said Tomasz Jedrzejczak, an analyst at Bank Handlowy brokerage.
